findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint now pages with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime" when optimized_pagination=true. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, key))) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first successful page raises TypeError while building the next cursor, and any non-zero cursor is compared to the datetime column as an int. The optimized path 500s for every superuser or global-access member who passes the flag; DateTimePaginator is the type that actually converts datetimes.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination raises instead of slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set (the audit-log path always passes True), a cursor with offset < 0 is sliced as queryset[negative:stop]. Django QuerySet rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and does not clamp or wrap. The comment that the ORM handles this and that it reaches rows past normal bounds is wrong, so the new code path 500s on any such cursor and does not implement the pagination it claims.

findings.title: SET segment keys are incompatible with the new ZSET commands
findings.body: process_spans now ZADDs span payloads and _load_segment_data ZSCANs them, while add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN. Keys already written by the previous sadd/sunionstore path are Redis SETs. The first ZADD, ZUNIONSTORE, or ZSCAN on those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so in-flight segments cannot be merged or flushed and span ingestion fails until those keys expire. There is no new key prefix or migration.

findings.title: Eviction count is not atomic with the ZADD and can over-delete
findings.body: Payloads are ZADDed in a separate pipeline, then each span runs this script, which ZPOPMINs down to 1000 using a count read inside the script. Two overlapping batches can each observe a count above 1000 and each pop span_count-1000 members, deleting more than the excess (including spans just inserted by the other batch). The cap is also a hardcoded 1000, while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (1001) is no longer enforced, and the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log was removed, so drops are silent and not configurable.

findings.title: Redirect walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep segments
findings.body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000 and still HSETs the span onto whatever set_span_id it reached. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are no longer joined to the real segment root; those spans are stored and flushed as a separate segment. The previous comment that this limit breaks joining was removed rather than the walk being fixed.

findings.title: No test covers insert-time eviction or zset merge
findings.body: The buffer tests only add the new end_timestamp_precise field to existing small trees. Nothing asserts that a segment larger than 1000 spans ZPOPMINs the lowest scores, that the root span is kept, or that zunionstore still merges redirect keys. A WRONGTYPE against leftover SET keys and over-eviction across batches would not be caught.
